info.title: AstroWay Calculation API
info.description: Professional astrology calculation API powered by Swiss Ephemeris. Compute natal charts, synastry, progressions, directions, transits, Human Design, and 80+ other calculation types via a simple REST API.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key for authentication. Include in X-Api-Key header.

timezoneOffset.description: Hours from UTC at the given moment, not minutes. Fractional zones are hours too: 5.5 for India, 5.75 for Nepal, -3.5 for Newfoundland. Defaults to 0, meaning UTC.

ayanamsa.description: Sidereal school by name. Lahiri when omitted. Equivalent to ayanamsaId; send either.

ChartInput.description: Birth data for a single natal chart. Required: date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:mm:ss), latitude and longitude in decimal degrees. The short forms lat, lon, lng and tz are rejected with 400 INVALID_FIELD; pass the full names. timezoneOffset is hours from UTC and defaults to 0, meaning UTC. city is a display label only: nothing here geocodes it, so it never stands in for coordinates.

EmptyBody.description: This endpoint reads nothing from the request body. Send {} (or any object, which is ignored).

latitude.description: Birth latitude. Required here: the whole document is computed from it.

ChartInputUnknownTime.description: Birth data where the clock time may be unknown. Either pass time (HH:mm:ss), or set timeUnknown: true and omit it. In the second case the response carries planets and aspects but no houses, angles or sect.

TwoChartUnknownTime.description: Pair of natal charts where either birth time may be unknown. A chart with timeUnknown: true contributes planets and cross-aspects but no houses, angles or overlays.

ArabicParts.description: Natal chart plus optional custom lot definitions; the built-in set is used when omitted.

HdTransits.description: Transit moment plus an optional natal date, time and offset to overlay the activations on.

Almuten.description: Natal chart plus optional custom terms and decans tables.

EssentialDignities.description: Natal chart plus optional custom terms and decans tables.

Hyleg.description: Natal chart plus the hyleg method and optional custom dignity tables.

Receptions.description: Natal chart plus optional custom terms and decans tables.

DispositionChains.description: Natal chart plus the dispositor mode (rulership or detriment) and the ruler set (classical or modern).

Firdaria.description: Natal chart plus the number of years of firdaria periods to return.

SymbolicDirections.description: Natal chart plus a target date and the directional key: one degree per year, the Naibod rate, or the arc of the progressed Sun.

NatalTarget.description: Natal chart plus a target date for time-based calculations: progressions, directions, profections, returns.

PrimaryDirections.description: Natal chart plus the directional rate in degrees per year (Naibod 0.9856353 by default), the age to search to, and the aspect angles to test.

ParallelAspects.description: Natal chart plus the declination orb in degrees.

MidpointTrees.description: Natal chart plus the orb in degrees used for midpoint trees and symmetries.

JaiminiDashaSummary.description: Natal chart plus the target date for the Jaimini dasha summary.

SadeSati.description: Natal chart plus the target date for the Sade Sati phase.

latitude.description: Birth latitude. Required: the lagna is what both schools prescribe from.

longitude.description: Birth longitude. Required: the lagna is what both schools prescribe from.

school.description: Prescription school. Both reach the same three gems (the trikona lords), and differ on what they withhold and on the ordering. The response always names the one used. Default: lagna-lord.

Gemstone.description: Birth data for a gemstone recommendation. Required: date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:mm:ss), latitude and longitude. Coordinates do NOT default to 0 here as they do on other chart endpoints: the whole answer is derived from the lagna, so an omitted pair is a 400 rather than a confident set of gems for 0N 0E.

latitude.description: Birth latitude. Required: the muntha starts at the natal lagna.

longitude.description: Birth longitude. Required: the muntha starts at the natal lagna.

year.description: Calendar year of the solar return. The year is entered on the birthday of that year, not on 1 January.

entryLatitude.description: Where the year is entered, if not the birthplace. Classically the residence on the birthday. Moves the annual ascendant and every house with it; the planets and the muntha do not move. Must be sent together with entryLongitude.

entryLongitude.description: Longitude of the year entry. Must be sent together with entryLatitude.

Varshaphal.description: Birth data plus a year, for the Tajika annual chart. Required: date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:mm:ss), latitude, longitude and year. Coordinates do NOT default to 0 here as they do on other chart endpoints. The chart is cast on the SIDEREAL solar return, which for an adult is many hours away from the tropical one and therefore a different ascendant.

stars.description: Star names from the Swiss Ephemeris catalogue. Default: the 36-star astrological set.

planets.description: Swiss Ephemeris planet ids. Default: 0-9, Sun through Pluto.

latitudeLimit.description: Search range either side of the equator, degrees. Default 60, which is the range Brady tabulates.

horizon.description: Which horizon counts as rising. `geometric` (default) is altitude 0, the semi-diurnal arc as written in Meeus. `apparent` puts it at -34 arcmin, where refraction lifts a body into view first. Worth about two degrees of paran latitude at mid-latitudes, and refraction also breaks the equator mirror that the geometric horizon has, so it is a choice rather than a detail.

StarParans.description: Birth data for star-planet parans. Coordinates are not used: a paran is a latitude, and which latitudes exist depends on the moment, not on where the native was born.

category.description: One of the 19 ACG life categories. The list is at GET /v1/acg/categories.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes to restrict the search to. Omit to search the whole bundled list.

minPopulation.description: Floor on city population. The bundled set starts at 15000, so a lower value changes nothing.

orbKm.description: How far a line reaches, kilometres. Default 1126, which is the 700 miles Jim Lewis used.

limit.description: How many cities to return. Default 25.

minSeparationKm.description: Keep returned cities at least this far apart, kilometres. Default 300. An ACG line is a curve, so without thinning the top of the ranking is the densest stretch of one line rather than a set of places. Set 0 to disable and see every city in score order.

sort.description: `net` (default) ranks on supportive minus challenging. `supportive` ignores the challenging side when ordering, though it is still reported.

AcgBestPlaces.description: Birth data plus a life category. Birth coordinates are optional and unused for the ranking: astrocartography lines are a property of the birth moment, not of the birth place.

TwoChart.description: Pair of natal charts for relationship calculations: synastry, composite, davison.

MultiChart.description: Group of 2-10 natal charts for collective calculations: group synastry, penta-chart, etc.

NatalWrapper.description: Wrapper { natal: ChartInput } used by endpoints that take a base natal plus extra parameters in flat fields.

post.description: Calculate a full natal chart: planets, house cusps, aspects, sect, and angular data for a given birth moment. When the birth time is unknown, send timeUnknown: true instead of time and the response carries planets and aspects with houses, angles and sect set to null, plus a timeUnknown block giving the range the Moon covers that day.
post.x-source: Standard Western natal chart conventions: Placidus houses (default), tropical zodiac, Sun-Moon-Asc Big Three. Engine: Swiss Ephemeris WASM (Astrodienst aloistr/swisseph) via shared @/core lib.

post.summary: Best places for a life category
post.description: Rank cities against the astrocartography lines of a chart for one of the 19 life categories. Distance to a line is computed from the body hour angle and altitude rather than against a discretised polyline, so it is exact: the distance to a horizon line IS the altitude in degrees of arc, and a meridian line offset is the hour angle times cos(latitude). Supportive and challenging totals are returned separately with every contributing line and its distance, so a strong-but-turbulent city is distinguishable from an average one. Bundled GeoNames set of 34,028 places above 15,000 people. **Not geocoding**: a smaller town is absent from the ranking rather than ranked poorly, and an arbitrary place name cannot be resolved.
post.x-source: Sky geometry is the same as /acg. Category weights and polarities from data/acg-categories.ts (audited 2026-07-26). Orb default 1126 km is the 700 miles Jim Lewis used. City data: GeoNames cities15000 under CC BY 4.0, provenance and trimming in api-calc/data/geonames/LICENSE.md; attribution ships in the response because a downstream integrator inherits the obligation. Distance geometry pinned by placing a synthetic body directly overhead (0 km to MC, 10008 km to the horizon) and by three named cities cross-checked against /acg-zones.

post.description: Latitudes where a fixed star and a planet are angular at the same moment, which is how Brady tabulates a paran: not a place, a latitude. Twelve event pairs per star and planet (rise, set, culminate, anticulminate, minus meridian against meridian, which is a shared right ascension rather than a paran). Each row carries the houses of the technique in plain form: which body does what, the latitude, and the meridian where it happens at this chart moment. Solved on hour angles rather than by intersecting map polylines, so the latitude is exact rather than quantised to the polyline step. `horizon` selects the geometric horizon (default) or the apparent one at -34 arcmin, measured at about two degrees of paran latitude at mid-latitudes.
post.x-source: Bernadette Brady, "Brady's Book of Fixed Stars" (1998) for the technique and for reporting a paran as a latitude; the astronomy is the standard semi-diurnal arc, Meeus "Astronomical Algorithms" ch. 15. The ecliptic-to-equatorial conversion stars need is pinned against Swiss Ephemeris by running the planets through it and comparing with SEFLG_EQUATORIAL. Every returned latitude is verified to put both bodies angular at one sidereal time, the meridian cases against their closed form, and the whole solver against the equator-mirror invariant. Brady's own worked Castor example is reproduced to within a degree.

post.description: The Tajika annual chart for one year of life. Cast on the moment the SIDEREAL Sun returns to its natal longitude, which for an adult sits many hours away from the tropical solar return and therefore on a different ascendant: the gap runs 0.4 h at age 1, 3.3 h at 10, 7.0 h at 20, 12.5 h at 36 and 17.2 h at 50. Returns the year entry to the second, the sidereal annual chart, the muntha (the natal lagna advanced one sign per completed year) with its house and lord, Panchavargiya bala for all seven grahas (griha, uchcha, hadda, drekkana, navamsa, summed and quartered into Vishwa out of 20), the five office bearers a year lord is chosen from, and five sahams. The year lord comes back twice, because the sources disagree: `varshesha` follows the Hayanaratna, which requires an aspect to the annual ascendant before strength is consulted and carries the reason it chose; `varsheshaByStrength` is the modern shortcut of taking the strongest candidate outright. Pass `entryLatitude`/`entryLongitude` to enter the year somewhere other than the birthplace, which moves the ascendant and the houses but not the planets or the muntha. Coordinates are required.
post.x-source: Balabhadra, *Hayanaratna* (1629) tr. Martin Gansten: munthaha 5.1, triplicity rulers 5.7, ruler of the year 5.8, orbs of light 3.1, saham rule 4.2. K. S. Charak, *A Textbook of Varshaphala*, for the Panchavargiya unit values and the strength-only year lord. The Egyptian bounds are cross-checked against a second, non-Tajika source. The year entry is exact by construction and asserted: the sidereal Sun is back on its natal longitude to under 1e-6 degrees from age 1 to 50. The saham engine and its added-sign correction are pinned to the two worked examples in the Hayanaratna itself. YELLOW is doctrinal: the year lord has two readings, only five of the circulated thirty-five sahams have a second source, and Mudda dasha is deliberately absent because the sources split on its first lord.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Alternative to Accept-Language for clients without header control.

parameters.name: X-Provider
parameters.description: Bring your own model key: the LLM provider that should run this completion. Send together with X-Provider-Key or the request is refused: a key with no provider bills us for tokens you meant to pay for, and a provider with no key would look like it worked. parameters.name: X-Provider-Key
parameters.description: Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Model
parameters.description: Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → llama-3.3-70b-versatile, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.

parameters.name: X-Provider
parameters.description: Bring your own model key: the LLM provider that should run this completion. Send together with X-Provider-Key or the request is refused: a key with no provider bills us for tokens you meant to pay for, and a provider with no key would look like it worked. The endpoint is fixed per provider on our side and is never taken from the request. There is no fallback to our own chain: if your key fails you get the provider's status and message. Applies only when `enrich: true` asks for the AI narrative.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Key
parameters.description: Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Model
parameters.description: Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → llama-3.3-70b-versatile, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.

parameters.name: X-Provider
parameters.description: Bring your own model key: the LLM provider that should run this completion. Send together with X-Provider-Key or the request is refused: a key with no provider bills us for tokens you meant to pay for, and a provider with no key would look like it worked. The endpoint is fixed per provider on our side and is never taken from the request. There is no fallback to our own chain: if your key fails you get the provider's status and message.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Key
parameters.description: Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Model
parameters.description: Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → llama-3.3-70b-versatile, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.

parameters.name: X-Provider
parameters.description: Bring your own model key: the LLM provider that should run this completion. Send together with X-Provider-Key or the request is refused: a key with no provider bills us for tokens you meant to pay for, and a provider with no key would look like it worked. The endpoint is fixed per provider on our side and is never taken from the request. There is no fallback to our own chain: if your key fails you get the provider's status and message.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Key
parameters.description: Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Model
parameters.description: Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → llama-3.3-70b-versatile, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.

get.description: Tool definitions for an agent framework, generated from the live OpenAPI document, so the schema a model fills is the schema the endpoint validates. `format=openai` (default) returns `{ type, function }` objects you can spread straight into a chat completion; `format=anthropic` returns `{ name, description, input_schema }`. The objects carry nothing of ours: how to call each tool lives in a separate `executors` map keyed by tool name, because an unexpected key inside a vendor tool object is a 400 at their end. `select` chooses what to hand over: the curated starter set by default, `all` for the catalogue, `group:Vedic` for one area, `paths:/chart,/synastry` for an explicit list; `q` filters within that, `limit` caps it (default 32, max 128, which is the OpenAI ceiling). Nothing truncates silently: `totalMatched`, `totalAvailable` and a note say what was left out. No auth is embedded in a tool, so send X-Api-Key on the call itself.
get.x-source: The OpenAPI document this API publishes, resolved: $ref inlined, allOf flattened with the override winning, and the OpenAPI 3.0 nullable spelling translated into a JSON Schema type union. Without that a model receives a schema its vendor rejects.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Which vendor contract the tool objects follow. `openai` returns `{ type, function }`, `anthropic` returns `{ name, description, input_schema }`.

parameters.name: select
parameters.description: What to hand over: `starter` (the curated set, the default), `all`, `group:<tag>` such as `group:Vedic`, or `paths:/chart,/synastry` for an explicit list. An unknown path is named in `notes` rather than dropped.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text filter applied within the selection, matched against path, summary, description and group.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many tools to return. The ceiling is the OpenAI limit of 128 functions per request; models degrade well before it. Anything left out is counted in `totalMatched`.

post.description: Translate one text into any of 21 languages with astrology-domain glossary pinning. Source defaults to English; pass source_lang to override. Credits: 15 + ceil(chars/40). Max 3000 chars.
post.x-source: Astro-aware machine translation across 21 languages via the ai.astroway.info LLM gateway, with a domain glossary (Vedic / Western / Tarot / Numerology / HD / marketing) pinning specialist terms (Dasha, Nakshatra, Ascendant, …) so they are not mistranslated. Numeric fields untouched.

parameters.name: X-Provider
parameters.description: Bring your own model key: the LLM provider that should run this completion. Send together with X-Provider-Key or the request is refused: a key with no provider bills us for tokens you meant to pay for, and a provider with no key would look like it worked. The endpoint is fixed per provider on our side and is never taken from the request. There is no fallback to our own chain: if your key fails you get the provider's status and message.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Key
parameters.description: Your own credential for X-Provider. Never logged, stored or cached: it travels in a header because the request body is hashed into two cache keys, and a BYOK turn bypasses both caches in each direction. A provider error that quotes the key back is redacted before it reaches our logs or your response. Such a turn costs 5 credits instead of the endpoint price, and only when a completion actually ran on your key.

parameters.name: X-Provider-Model
parameters.description: Optional model id, overriding the default for that provider. Defaults: openai → gpt-4o-mini, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-5, google → gemini-2.5-flash, groq → llama-3.3-70b-versatile, mistral → mistral-large-latest, openrouter → meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, deepseek → deepseek-chat, together → meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo.
